prompt: Describe metallic bonding and use it to explain why metals are malleable.
markscheme: Electrostatic attraction between a lattice of cations and a sea of delocalised electrons **(A1)**; layers of cations can slide over each other without breaking the bonding, because the delocalised electrons still hold them **(R1)**

prompt: Which metal has the highest melting point?
markscheme: **C.** Metallic bonding is stronger with higher ionic charge and smaller ionic radius: Al³⁺ is small and highly charged, giving more delocalised electrons and stronger attraction.

prompt: Explain why transition metals such as iron have higher melting points and densities than group 1 metals.
markscheme: Both 4s and 3d electrons can be delocalised, giving more delocalised electrons per atom and stronger metallic bonding **(R1)**; their atoms are also smaller and more massive, so they pack more closely **(R1)**
